content.text: undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; breast cancer or a history of breast cancer (except selected patients treated for metastatic disease); estrogen-dependent neoplasia; active or past DVT or PE; active or past arterial thromboembolic disease (eg, stroke, MI); hepatic impairment or disease; protein C, protein S or antithrombin deficiency or other thrombophilia.

unopposed estrogen raises the risk of endometrial cancer in a woman with a uterus. Estrogen-alone therapy should not be used to prevent cardiovascular disease or dementia; WHIMS found a higher risk of probable dementia in postmenopausal women 65 and older on estrogen alone.
